entities.evidence: Lamech recalls the sevenfold vengeance promised in Genesis 4:15 for anyone who kills Cain, Abel’s brother.
The speaker addresses his wives Adah and Zillah in Genesis 4:23. Genesis 4:18–19 identifies their husband as the son of Methushael.

review.translation: [For|0] [Cain|3] [will be avenged|2] [seven times over|1], [and Lamech|4] {will be avenged} [seventy|5]-[seven|6] {times over}!”

analysis.evidence: Lamech gives the ground for his boast by invoking Cain’s sevenfold vengeance. The parallel clause וְלֶמֶךְ שִׁבְעִים וְשִׁבְעָה carries over the verb יֻקַּם and raises the figure to seventy-seven for Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שִׁבְעָתַיִם modifies יֻקַּם, specifying how fully Cain is avenged. Lamech contrasts Cain’s sevenfold vengeance with his own seventy-sevenfold vengeance.
analysis.morphology: Feminine dual absolute form used adverbially.

analysis.evidence: קָיִן is the subject of the passive יֻקַּם. Vengeance will be exacted on Cain’s behalf, and שִׁבְעָתַיִם specifies its measure as sevenfold.
analysis.morphology: Hophal imperfect, third person masculine singular

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Cain with its etymology left open pending evidence.
draft.definition: Cain, the son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:1 names Eve’s son קַיִן. Genesis 4:2 identifies Abel as his brother and names Cain again when describing his work.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 4:24, קָיִן is the subject of יֻקַּם, “will be avenged.” Lamech contrasts sevenfold vengeance for Cain with seventy-sevenfold vengeance for himself, recalling the protection promised to Cain in Genesis 4:15.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the pausal form קָיִן, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Abel’s brother.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לֶמֶךְ. The text gives no derivation for the name.
draft.definition: Lamech is a masculine personal name. Here it designates the son of Methushael.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:18 names Lamech as Methushael’s son. In 4:23–24 he addresses his wives and names himself alongside Cain.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 4:23 identifies Lamech as the speaker. In 4:24, לֶמֶךְ parallels קָיִן as the subject of the understood verb יֻקַּם, “will be avenged.” Cain will be avenged sevenfold, and Lamech seventy-sevenfold.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular proper noun.
analysis.sense: Lamech, son of Methushael and speaker of the saying.

analysis.evidence: In שִׁבְעִים וְשִׁבְעָה, the marked word supplies the seventy and the following word adds seven. Together they express seventy-sevenfold vengeance for Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, common to both genders, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: שִׁבְעִים וְשִׁבְעָה means “seventy and seven.” The marked numeral supplies the final seven in the count of seventy-seven times, set against Cain’s sevenfold vengeance.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus שִׁבְעָה, a masculine singular absolute cardinal numeral.
